# Physics, code, and the physics of materials
I study how matter behaves one atom at a time — and I build the software that makes that research faster for everyone.

## The short version
## Hello! I'm Soumyajit, a physics postgraduate who codes
I'm a Physics postgraduate at the National Institute of Technology Silchar, specialising in computational condensed matter physics. My current research uses density functional theory to study two-dimensional materials — probing their band structures, optical response and potential for optoelectronic applications.

Beyond research, I'm an active scientific software developer. I created VaspViz , a PyQt6 desktop suite for post-processing VASP calculations, along with several smaller tools — because I believe good software should shave hours off a researcher's week.

When I'm not parsing vasprun.xml files, you'll find me exploring Linux, writing about science on my blog, or following football. The fastest way to reach me is dsoumyajit295@gmail.com Copy .

The hero pairs the bio text with a real interactive terminal: it auto-types an intro, then accepts keyboard input (help, whoami, research, projects, education, skills, contact, cv, theme, date, echo, history, clear; Up/Down history, Tab completion, clickable links in output).

[Download CV] -> docs/SOUMYAJIT_DAS_CV.pdf
[LinkedIn] -> https://www.linkedin.com/in/soumyajit-das-40a1851b8/

# Research first, then the tools
I'm a Physics M.Sc. student first — so this page opens with the two reports behind my degree: the ab-initio DFT study of ZrS 2 and ZrSe 2 for NIT Silchar, and a summer of first-principles calculations at IISER Kolkata. The software I build to speed that kind of research up follows below.

## Research Reports
Two documents, two institutions — the dissertation and the internship my Physics M.Sc. stands on. Click a cover to read the front page up close.

### Ab-initio DFT study of monolayer & bilayer ZrS 2 and ZrSe 2
My M.Sc. dissertation: a density-functional theory study of the two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides ZrS 2 and ZrSe 2 — from relaxed crystal structures through to band structures and density of states. The through-line is the monolayer–bilayer comparison: what a second layer, and the van der Waals gap it opens between the two, does to a 2D material's electronic structure.

Structural relaxation · Band structure · Density of states · Monolayer vs bilayer · Interlayer vdW gap · 2D TMDs

VASP · Ab-initio DFT · 2D materials

### First-Principles DFT Calculations on Crystalline Materials
The report of my summer at the Department of Physical Sciences, IISER Kolkata (May–July 2025): first-principles calculations on crystalline materials, worked through two codes — plane-wave VASP and the all-electron Elk. Total energies, relaxed geometries, band structures and density of states: the full pipeline from a raw crystal structure to physics you can plot.

Total energies · Relaxed geometries · Band structure · Density of states · Two-code workflow

VASP · Elk · First-principles DFT · Summer 2025

## Software Projects
Tools I built so that research — mine and everyone else's — moves faster.

Built with help from AI: developed with AI coding assistants as a pair-programmer for boilerplate, debugging and documentation, while the physics, architecture and final decisions stayed mine.

### VaspViz
A cross-platform desktop application I built with PyQt6 for analyzing and visualizing VASP (Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package) output. VaspViz turns raw first-principles data into publication-ready figures — band structures, density of states, optical spectra and more — without writing a single line of script. What used to be an afternoon of matplotlib plumbing becomes a few clicks.

Band structure · DOS · Fat bands · Wannier90 · Optical spectra · 3D POSCAR viewer · CHGCAR rendering · EOS fitting · Convergence monitor

Python · PyQt6 · Matplotlib · NumPy · SciPy · pyqtgraph

### WallPrx
A fast, distraction-free platform for discovering high-resolution desktop and mobile wallpapers. Curated collections, instant preview and one-click download — a clean, ad-free experience built with a mobile-first responsive interface.

Curated collections · Instant preview · One-click download · 4K & mobile · Ad-free · Mobile-first UI

HTML5 · CSS3 · JavaScript · Responsive UI

### Theorem
A clean, modern equation editor for students, teachers and researchers: type LaTeX, see perfectly typeset maths instantly, and export it as a crisp image for assignments, papers and slides. No clutter — just beautiful equations, the moment you finish typing them.

Live rendering · Crisp image export · Fractions, matrices & align · Assignments, papers & slides

LaTeX · Web app · Works in the browser

## Have an idea or found a bug?
Both projects are open source — issues, ideas and pull requests are welcome.

# Writing about science & technology
Notes on physics, mathematics and the tools I build — written for students, teachers and the endlessly curious.

## Latest posts
### Theorem: A Modern LaTeX Equation Editor for Students, Teachers and Researchers
Clean, professional equations for assignments, papers and presentations — how I built Theorem, a live LaTeX editor that renders maths instantly and exports it as crisp images.

### The Most Beautiful Equation in Mathematics
Euler's identity links five fundamental constants in a single line. A look at why physicists and mathematicians call it the most beautiful equation ever written.

### Top 5 Revolutionary Physics Equations
From Newton to Schrödinger — five equations that reshaped how we understand the universe, and the stories of the people who wrote them.

## About the blog
Sci-Tech Science is my Blogger-hosted corner of the internet, running since 2024. Expect physics explainers without the jargon, mathematics with actual intuition, and behind-the-scenes stories of the tools I build — like Theorem, the LaTeX equation editor.
